questions.question:
gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules. Add them?

D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count on main, starting /plan-ceo-review of PLAN.md (saved project views).
ELI10: gstack has many skills (/investigate, /ship, /qa...). A short routing section in CLAUDE.md tells Claude which skill to reach for when you describe a task in plain words, so you don't have to remember slash names. This is a one-time setup, separate from the plan review.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without it, skills only fire when you type them explicitly; with it, a few lines get appended to CLAUDE.md and committed.
Recommendation: A because routing is cheap and makes the rest of gstack discoverable.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Plain-language requests like "find this bug" auto-route to the right skill
  ✅ One-time append and commit; nothing else in the repo changes
  ❌ Adds ~20 lines to CLAUDE.md; commit happens after plan mode ends since edits are frozen now
B) No thanks, invoke manually
  ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as-is for this fixture repo
  ✅ Re-enable any time with one config command
  ❌ Skills stay invisible unless you type the slash name
Net: Discoverability vs. an untouched CLAUDE.md.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Plain-language requests auto-route to the matching gstack skill. ✅ One-time append and commit. ❌ Adds ~20 lines to CLAUDE.md; the write waits until plan mode ends.

options.label: No thanks, invoke manually
options.description: ✅ CLAUDE.md stays untouched. ✅ Re-enable later with one config command. ❌ Skills only fire when typed explicitly.

questions.question:
D2 — Which review mode for the saved project views plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count on main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved views: table + CRUD + picker).
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. Expansion means I pitch bigger versions of the feature. Selective means I harden what you wrote and offer add-ons one at a time for you to accept or reject. Hold means I only stress-test what is there. Reduction means I look for what to cut. The plan is an added capability on an existing task list, about ~12 changed files (estimate; the app code is not in this repo).
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too big a mode and you get pitched a views platform you did not ask for; too small and the schema ships without a visibility column, which turns team-shared views into a migration plus permission rework in six months.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the plan's premise ("team members repeatedly recreate filters") likely covers shared filters too, and a one-column decision now is much cheaper than a migration later, but that is your call per item, not a blanket expansion.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
  ✅ Hardens the current scope first (HOLD checks run in full), then offers each add-on separately
  ✅ Surfaces the visibility-column and filter-versioning forks while they are still one-column decisions
  ❌ A few more questions than HOLD; each add-on is its own accept/defer/skip
B) HOLD SCOPE
  ✅ Fastest path: maximum rigor on exactly the four approach bullets you wrote
  ✅ No scope debate; every finding is about failure paths, tests, observability
  ❌ Leaves the shared-views fork unexamined; you may pay for it as a migration later
C) SCOPE EXPANSION
  ✅ Aims at the 12-month ideal: shared views, defaults, dirty indicators, shareable links
  ✅ Best if the pilot goal is to make views the primary way people navigate tasks
  ❌ ~12 files becomes 20+; the two-week pilot metric gets muddied by feature count
D) SCOPE REDUCTION
  ✅ Strips to the minimum that proves reuse in the pilot (e.g. create + list + apply only)
  ✅ Smallest diff, fastest to ship
  ❌ Update/delete are cheap and their absence makes the pilot data worse (stale views nobody can remove)
Net: How much of the 12-month ideal you want to decide now versus after the pilot.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Hardens current scope first, then offers each add-on separately for accept/defer/skip. ✅ Surfaces the visibility-column and filter-versioning forks while cheap. ❌ A few more questions than HOLD.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: ✅ Maximum rigor on exactly the four approach bullets; fastest. ✅ Findings focus on failure paths, tests, observability. ❌ Shared-views fork stays unexamined; possible migration later.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: ✅ Aims at the 12-month ideal: shared views, defaults, dirty indicator, shareable links. ✅ Best if views become the primary navigation. ❌ ~12 files becomes 20+; pilot metric gets muddied.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: ✅ Minimum that proves reuse: create + list + apply. ✅ Smallest diff. ❌ Dropping update/delete leaves stale views nobody can remove, hurting pilot data.
